questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. Lying in bed waiting

B. For the postman to bring

C. Him news of a legacy

D. Luck keeps on
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with "Luck keeps on," which is correctly indicated by **part (D).**
 
• Following this, "lying in bed waiting" **(A)** logically continues the sequence, describing the action that luck finds the person doing.
 
• **The next part,** "for the postman to bring" **(B)** continues with what the person is waiting for.
 
• **Ending with** "him news of a legacy" **(C)** completes the sentence by stating what the postman is expected to bring.

Therefore, the correct answer is **DABC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (BDAC):** This option starts with "for the postman to bring lying in bed waiting," which disrupts the logical flow of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3 (BDCA):** This option starts with "for the postman to bring him news of a legacy," which misses out on the original focus and sequence of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 (ADBC):** This option starts with "lying in bed waiting luck keeps on," which makes the sentence grammatically incorrect and confusing.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

She met my cousin, __whose she later married__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment “whose she later married” is incorrect because **“whose” **is a possessive pronoun that should be used to show ownership, not as an object of a verb.
 
• The correct pronoun here should be “whom” since it acts as the object of the verb **“married.”**
 
• Option 1,** "whom she later married,"** correctly uses the objective case pronoun **"whom."**
 
• Options 2 and 3 are grammatically incorrect, and option 4 is invalid as the given sentence requires a substitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“She met my cousin,** whom** she later married.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Using the correct pronoun in a sentence ensures clarity and grammatical accuracy.
 
• "Whom" is used when referring to the object of a verb or preposition, which is the situation in this sentence.
 
• The clause “whom she later married” is a defining relative clause that gives us essential information about “my cousin.”

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The child was testing the patience of her mother.

options.text: The patience of her mother had been tested by the child.
The patience of her mother was being tested by the child.
The patience of her mother was tested by the child.
Her mother was tested by the patient child.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the **passive sentence.**
 
• The original sentence is: **"The child was testing the patience of her mother."**
 
• To convert this to passive voice,** "the patience of her mother"** (the object) becomes the subject.
 
• The verb "was testing" is changed to **"was being tested"** to match the continuous tense in passive voice.
 
• The doer "by the child" is added at the end.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“The patience of her mother was being tested by the child.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The patience of her mother had been tested by the child." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
 
• **Option 3:** "The patience of her mother was tested by the child." – Incorrect tense (simple past passive).
 
• **Option 4:** "Her mother was tested by the patient child." – Incorrect and misleading.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Shanky said, 'I'll be disposing of the old iPhone next Wednesday'.

options.text: Shanky said that he would be disposing of the old iPhone the following Wednesday.
Shanky said that he would be disposing off the old iPhone the following Wednesday.
Shanky said that he would have been disposing of the old iPhone the following Wednesday.
Shanky said that he will have been disposing off the old iPhone the following Wednesday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** Shanky said, 'I'll be disposing of the old iPhone next Wednesday.'
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Tense Change:** "I'll be disposing" (future continuous) changes to "he would be disposing" (future continuous in indirect speech).
 
• **Time Expression:** "next Wednesday" changes to "the following Wednesday" in indirect speech.
 
• **Pronoun Change:** "I'll" changes to "he" to match the third-person perspective in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors in Other Options:**
 
 
• Option 2 has an incorrect form "disposing off" instead of "disposing of."
 
• Option 3 uses the incorrect tense "would have been disposing" which changes the meaning.
 
• Option 4 uses the incorrect tense "will have been disposing off," which is also grammatically incorrect.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *“Shanky said that he would be disposing of the old iPhone the following Wednesday.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Shanky said that he would be disposing off the old iPhone the following Wednesday." – This option is incorrect due to the incorrect verb form "disposing off."
 
• **Option 3:** "Shanky said that he would have been disposing of the old iPhone the following Wednesday." – This option uses an incorrect tense which alters the meaning.
 
• **Option 4:** "Shanky said that he will have been disposing off the old iPhone the following Wednesday." – This option is incorrect due to both the incorrect tense and the incorrect verb form "disposing off."

• To convert to active voice, the subject** "Rupesh" **should come first, followed by the verb and the object.
 
• Ensure the question format is maintained with appropriate auxiliary verb "did" for past tense questions.
